topic: Antibiotic prescribing in upper respiratory tract infection

audits.title: Antibiotic use in acute upper respiratory tract infections and uncomplicated lacerations in the Gaza Strip: clinical audit and re-audit.
audits.standard: Best international standards of antibiotic prescribing: no antibiotics for acute upper respiratory tract infections or uncomplicated lacerations

cycle1.result: Antibiotics prescribed to 52 (87%) of 60 patients with acute URTI and to all 59 patients whose lacerations were sutured (98% of 60).

audits.intervention: One-year action plan focusing on education of health-care providers and patients.

cycle2.result: Antibiotics prescribed to 43 (71%) patients with acute URTI (p=0.002) and to 50 (84%) with uncomplicated lacerations.

audits.other_findings: Only 25 (42%) of URTI patients had throat examinations; 52 (87%) of laceration patients believed antibiotics accelerate healing.
audits.citation: Alfaqawi M, Abuowda Y, Böttcher B, Alserr K, Elmassry AE. Antibiotic use in acute upper respiratory tract infections and uncomplicated lacerations in the Gaza Strip: clinical audit and re-audit. Lancet. 2021;398 Suppl 1:S7. doi:10.1016/s0140-6736(21)01493-8. PMID: 34227989.

audits.title: Delayed antibiotic prescribing to reduce antibiotic use: an urgent care practice change.
audits.standard: CDC adult URI treatment guidelines for antibiotic use

cycle1.result: Chart audits showed antibiotics routinely prescribed for URI without patient instruction; comparative group n = 598.

audits.intervention: Implementation of CDC URI guidelines with delayed antibiotic prescribing and follow-up phone calls 10 days after discharge.

cycle2.result: Antibiotic usage rates decreased by 12% in 30 days (U = 247, p = 0.023).

audits.other_findings: High patient satisfaction was maintained; most urgent care sites lacked an antibiotic stewardship plan.
audits.citation: Tonazzi S, Prenovost L, Scheuermann S. Delayed antibiotic prescribing to reduce antibiotic use: an urgent care practice change. BMJ Open Qual. 2022;11(1):e001513. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2021-001513. PMID: 35264330.

audits.title: Evaluation and optimization of antibiotic usage in upper respiratory tract infections in children at a tertiary care outpatient department: A clinical audit.
audits.standard: Benchmark antibiotic prescription rate for URTI; Indian Ministry of Health URTI guidelines
audits.setting: Paediatric outpatient department, Tata Main Hospital, Jamshedpur; tertiary care

cycle1.result: Baseline antibiotic prescription rate 14.7%, ranging 4.1% to 53.1% between consultants.

audits.intervention: Discussions, presentations, posters, guidelines on URTI aetiology and antibiotic indications, with monitoring and feedback to consultants.

cycle2.result: Average antibiotic prescription rate fell to 8.7% (40.8% reduction); azithromycin use fell from 21.2% to 14.4%.

audits.other_findings: Amoxicillin-clavulanate and amoxicillin remained the most prescribed; high-prescribing consultants also reduced.
audits.citation: Mishra S, Srivastava P, Sunder S, Mishra AK, Tanti SK. Evaluation and optimization of antibiotic usage in upper respiratory tract infections in children at a tertiary care outpatient department: A clinical audit. Indian J Pharmacol. 2022;54(1):13-18. doi:10.4103/ijp.ijp_373_21. PMID: 35343202.

audits.title: Improvement of antibiotic use in sore throat, tonsillitis and acute otitis media in Palestine: a prospective full cycle audit.
audits.standard: International guidelines on antibiotic prescribing for sore throat, tonsillitis and acute otitis media

cycle1.result: Inadequate adherence to international guidelines (baseline figures not given).

audits.intervention: Surveys, oral presentations and development of mobile/web applications.

cycle2.result: Correct direct antibiotic prescriptions +6.5%, correct backup prescriptions +44.4%, correct no-antibiotic prescriptions +63.4%, correct antibiotic choice +41.4%, correct frequency/dose/duration +13.3%.

audits.other_findings: 297 cases across both phases: tonsillitis 56.9%, sore throat 29.6%, acute otitis media 13.5%. Trend towards second-line antibiotics noted.
audits.citation: AbuMohsen H, Abusheikha M. Improvement of antibiotic use in sore throat, tonsillitis and acute otitis media in Palestine: a prospective full cycle audit. J Infect Dev Ctries. 2022;16(12):1826-1834. doi:10.3855/jidc.17245. PMID: 36753648.

audits.title: Intermittent Education and Audit and Feedback Reduce Inappropriate Prescribing of Oral Third-Generation Cephalosporins for Pediatric Upper Respiratory Tract Infections.
audits.standard: American Academy of Pediatrics guidelines for bacterial upper respiratory tract infections; aim to reduce inappropriate oral third-generation cephalosporins by 15% in one year
audits.setting: Paediatric ambulatory care clinic (Clinic A) in a Houston network, with Texas Children's Hospital stewardship team

cycle1.result: 72% (231/322) of oral third-generation cephalosporin prescriptions did not align with AAP guidelines.

audits.intervention: PDSA cycles over one year: one educational session, three individual audit and feedback sessions and one group feedback session.

cycle2.result: Mean inappropriate prescribing fell from 72% to 45% (absolute reduction 27%).

audits.other_findings: No reduction at four control clinics; improvements were maintained despite less participation.
audits.citation: Taylor M, Liechti S, Palazzi D. Intermittent Education and Audit and Feedback Reduce Inappropriate Prescribing of Oral Third-Generation Cephalosporins for Pediatric Upper Respiratory Tract Infections. Jt Comm J Qual Patient Saf. 2021;47(4):250-257. doi:10.1016/j.jcjq.2020.12.003. PMID: 33446441.
